target_customer: Enterprises, governments and law enforcement buying threat intelligence and dark web monitoring
problem: Organizations cannot see leaked credentials and attacks on the dark web and surface web early; Cyble scrapes these sources and uses AI to deliver early warning.
business_model: Enterprise SaaS subscription for threat intelligence platforms (Cyble Vision, Cyble Hawk)

founders.name: Beenu Arora
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch says he bootstrapped the company for its first two years.

founders.name: Manish Chachada
founders.background_notes: YC page bio: over 15 years in finance, accounting and fundraising.

technical_complexity.rationale: Large scale crawling of dark web and surface web sources with indexing and alerting; standard engineering with hard data collection.

defensibility.rationale: Accumulated breach and dark web data and customer integrations; a crowded market with well-funded rivals limits defensibility.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Established vendors already sold similar threat intelligence; no source found of them copying Cyble, and Cyble kept raising through 2023.

market_need_then: Rising breaches and ransomware in 2020 and 2021 and demand for dark web monitoring; the company launched consumer breach check AmIBreached.com before enterprise products.

identity.logo: Stylized blue eagle introduced in a 2021 logo refresh
identity.visual_style: Security brand with bird theme (Cyble Hawk)

branding.brand_signature: Eagle logo and hawk product naming

rebrands.why: CEO said the new logo reflects the company's vision and mission and the next stage of growth

branding.community_and_virality: Cyble Research Labs publishes threat reports and AmIBreached.com drew public use; no merch found.

brand_strength.rationale: Moderate trade press recognition but crowded with larger incumbents; trademarks exist for Cyble Vision and Cyble Hawk.

outcome_analysis: Cyble raised a 4 million seed in April 2021, a 10 million Series A in February 2022 and a 24 million Series B in July 2023, reaching about 38.6 million raised and a team near 200. It grew in a crowded threat intelligence market by launching new products such as Cyble Hawk and Vision. No exit or shutdown found, so it appears to be a funded growth-stage company.
